notes:
Scope covered: opener/ender scenes explicit for all runs 1-12 (fallback rotation retired), day-open cutscenes for days 1-10, tutorial-intro/tutorial-outro framing, and a DAY_LINES audit. Zero art orders filed (brief sets zero art budget); every beat reuses SISTER, FATHER, COMPANION, STILL_LOCKED, STILL_BENCH, STILL_COUNTER, STILL_OPEN tokens only. Design notes and one ledger conflict below.

1) OPENERS 2-6 are revisions, not rewrites: each existing beat is kept verbatim and a single new sister beat is inserted BEFORE it, so every opener 1-12 now carries at least two sister beats per the brief. Each new beat only riffs on material the corresponding prior run's ENDER already revealed to Rhea (never ahead of the ledger's table): opener 3 references ender 2's shaking hands, opener 4 references ender 3's 'it waited', opener 5 references ender 4's 'it paces you', opener 6 references ender 5's 'kind first, why kind'. Opener 2 is pure protective-fear escalation off run 1's strain scare (no reveal dependency). Openers 7-12 are wholly new, replacing the fallback cycle, and give Rhea a visible arc: 7 (suspicion building, pre-power-bills), 8 (vindicated by her own math, still closing on the old 'so does my theory' line), 9 (first tender gesture toward the room, post run-8 renunciation), 10 (grappling with 'it' no longer feeling like the right word), 11 (fear gone, naming it herself), 12 (open anticipation of what happens if he gets through). This directly answers the brief's complaint that the arc 'stalls at run 8'.

2) ENDERS 9-12: SECTOR/LEDGER CONFLICT FLAGGED. The brief asks enders 9-12 to continue the sector sequence toward sector 9, landing sector 9 at run 10 or later. Ledger Resolved ruling 3 (2026-07-25) hard-forbids this: sector 8 is Patch's own withheld grief and sector 9 is the finale message's raw material, and 'Forbids either sector appearing in the run 2-8 schedule or any run 9+ fallback cycle.' The reveal-schedule rules repeat this explicitly. I did not write sector 8 or 9 as numbered fragments anywhere. Instead, enders 9-12 are bespoke (not the literal fallback function, per the brief's 'no fallback rotation') but stay inside the ledger's own established convention for runs 9+: 'SECTOR SCAN: NO NEW DATA. ECHO FOLLOWS.' followed by a verbatim replay of an already-unlocked sector's father lines (sector 1 at run 9, sector 6 at run 10, sector 4 at run 11, sector 2 at run 12, chosen for thematic fit, not new content). Every one of these gets a brand new SISTER beat that deepens her arc emotionally (per item 1 above) without adding a single new ground-truth fact, consistent with the ledger's own note that 'knowledge plateaus at the run-8 state until a finale win.' If the intent is truly to tease sector 8 or 9 before the finale, that needs an explicit new ruling from the Loremaster/user overriding Resolved ruling 3; I am flagging it, not implementing it.

3) DAY-OPEN SCENES (days 1-10) are deliberately run-count-agnostic in a way the openers/enders are not: since the same day-open-N plays on every run's day N regardless of run count, it cannot safely carry any of Rhea's evolving virus-theory language (a run-1 day-3 and a run-11 day-3 use the same scene, and her belief state is wildly different between them). So all ten stay in the 'daily shop rhythm' register: till, spike, ledger, register drawer, named customer devices, Rhea's logistics voice, and only bare physical, belief-neutral facts about the back room (a curtain that does not move, a padlock catching light). Day-open-10 is the one exception the brief calls out by name ('replaces the finale-door copy as the morning frame'); it still stays neutral, using only the already-established, belief-neutral phrase 'the back room settles up' rather than asserting any theory. Flagging this design choice explicitly in case the Orchestrator expected day-opens to carry run-specific reveals; I judged that unsafe given they are not run-keyed.

4) DAYLINE AUDIT: I checked all 9 existing DAY_LINES against the new day-open-1..9 scenes for clashes. None found; every existing line's content (tickets, strain carryover, pacing, halfway quiet, coffee, hard cases, strain-as-budget, last day) is already consistent with its matching day-open scene. Zero dayline items included this cycle; none needed changing.

5) TUTORIAL framing is new and slots in chronologically BEFORE run-open-1: tutorial-intro is the player reaching for the back room before the shop rules even exist (Rhea catches him at the curtain, DAD.LOG is found unopened), the scripted dive is mechanically owned by the Orchestrator (0/200 wins), tutorial-outro shows the room resealing and Rhea drawing the hard line. This makes run-open-1's existing 'One rule, the machine stays locked' read as a reiteration of a boundary just tested, not a first mention, without needing to touch run-open-1 itself.

6) HOUSEKEEPING FYI for the Loremaster, not mine to fix: I grepped the live repo before writing anything (per my own past workflow notes) and found ledger.md's 'Note - shipped/canon realignment status' section (around its own line 173) still describes story.ts's run-end-3 sector 2 line as outstanding and pending integration, but the shipped story.ts file no longer contains that line at all; it already reads 'This bench light is the only one on the block... The shop and I have some talking to do,' matching ground truth point 1. bible.md itself is already clean, no dust or Overby references anywhere in it or in the shipped game repo. The ledger's own status note looks stale and could use a cleanup pass; I left lore/* untouched since that is not my file to write.

items.notes: Revision: existing system and sister beats kept verbatim (beats 1 and 3 below). One new sister beat inserted at position 2, deepening the protective-fear reaction to run 1's strain scare. No new ground-truth content.

beats.speaker: system
lines: RUN 2.
The lock is where you left it. So is the debt.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: You scared me last night. Whatever is wrong with that machine does not get to take my brother too.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: You went back in. I heard the fans spin up at two in the morning.
It is a virus. Viruses do not need your whole night.
Customers first. Then do whatever it is you are doing.

items.notes: Revision: beats 1 and 3 kept verbatim. New sister beat 2 references the shaking hands from run 2's ender only, nothing further ahead.

beats.speaker: system
lines: RUN 3.
The bench knows your weight now.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: You slept maybe two hours. I counted the mug rings on the bench. That is how I know.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: You keep going back. Dad had that same look.
Same hours, too. I am not saying anything. I am just saying.

items.notes: Revision: beats 1 and 3 kept verbatim. New sister beat 2 references her own line from run 3's ender ('it waited... please do not tell me it waited'), a callback not a new reveal.

beats.speaker: system
lines: RUN 4.
The shop opens anyway. It always opens anyway.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: I keep thinking about the word waited. I should not have said it out loud.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: I stood outside the back room last night. Just listening.
It hums different when you are in there. I hate that I know that.

items.notes: Revision: beats 1 and 3 kept verbatim. New sister beat 2 references her own line from run 4's ender ('it paces you... viruses do not pace anybody').

beats.speaker: system
lines: RUN 5.
Three tickets on the spike. One padlock in the dark.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: It paces you. I wrote that down and then read it back to myself about six times.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: I oiled the hinges on the back door. Do not read into it.
Three tickets today. Eat something first.

items.notes: Revision: beats 1 and 3 kept verbatim (still STILL_COUNTER on beat 3 unchanged). New sister beat 2 references her own line from run 5's ender ('it learns... kind first, why kind').

beats.speaker: system
lines: RUN 6.
The clutter shrinks a little more every week. The padlock never has.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Kind first, then it takes you apart. What kind of virus plays nice on purpose?

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Dad used to come out of that room smiling. I forgot that until this week.
Go on, then. Customers first. Room later.

items.notes: New, replaces the old fallback rotation slot. Rhea is pre-power-bills here (that reveal is her own ender 7 line); she is only noticing behavior, not yet vindicated by evidence.

beats.speaker: system
lines: RUN 7.
The shop opens anyway.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: I keep hearing you talk back to it. Not shouting. Talking.
I do not know what kind of person does that for a virus, but here we are.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Coffee is on the bench. It is even fresh.
Come back up this time. I mean it.

items.notes: New, replaces the old fallback rotation slot. Sister beat 2 is her own vindication after doing the power-bill math (matches run 7's ender). Beat 3 is the old shipped 'so does my theory' fallback line, kept as the closer.

beats.speaker: system
lines: RUN 8.
The spike is full. The room is patient.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: I did the math twice, hoping I would get a different number. I did not.
Whatever he was doing back there, he paid for it himself. Every month. Nobody made him.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: That lock looks looser every week. So does my theory.
Go earn the rent first.

items.notes: New. First run after run 8's renunciation ('I think it has been waiting'). First tender, deliberate gesture toward the room, played light. No new ground-truth content, per the ledger's plateau note.

beats.speaker: system
lines: RUN 9.
The spike refills. It always does.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: I left something at the door this morning. Do not ask me why.
If it really is just waiting, I figure waiting is easier with coffee.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Go on, before it gets cold.
The coffee. I meant the coffee.

items.notes: New. Rhea grapples with 'it' no longer feeling like the right word, without reaching for a name (she never learns Patch's name pre-finale, per the ledger).

beats.speaker: system
lines: RUN 10.
Ten times now. The lock has not moved. Neither have you.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: I stood at the curtain again last night. Did not touch it. Just stood there.
It feels wrong to keep calling it that. I do not have a better word yet.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Anyway. Three tickets. The world outside that curtain still needs fixing.
Go.

items.notes: New. Fear gone, replaced by something closer to patience. A self-aware callback to 'around run six' rather than a new fact.

beats.speaker: system
lines: RUN 11.
The padlock. The curtain. The same morning, again.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: I am not scared walking past that door anymore. I noticed this morning.
I do not know when that happened. Somewhere around run six, maybe. I was not paying attention.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Three tickets. Go be the good half of this shop for a few hours.
Then go be whatever the other half of you is doing in there.

items.notes: New. Closes the 7-12 arc on open anticipation, priming the player for a finale attempt without asserting one is coming this run.

beats.speaker: system
lines: RUN 12.
The book resets. The padlock does not.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Twelve of these now. I have stopped asking when you will stop.
I have started asking what happens when you finally get through.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Go find out, then.
I will keep the coffee hot. Same as every time.

items.notes: New, replaces fallback rotation. Sector conflict: see top-level notes item 2. System and father beats are a verbatim echo of sector 1 (ender 2), framed with the ledger's own 'SECTOR SCAN: NO NEW DATA. ECHO FOLLOWS.' convention, not a new numbered sector. Strain-zero beat added mechanically by the Orchestrator, not included here.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: You are getting up slower every time. Or I am getting more scared every time. Hard to tell which anymore.
I want to believe it lets you through eventually. I did not expect to be the one hoping.

beats.speaker: system
lines: SECTOR SCAN: NO NEW DATA.
ECHO FOLLOWS.

beats.speaker: father
lines: Hold the iron like a pencil, not a hammer. There.
See? The joint holds because you were patient with it.
Most things do.

items.notes: New, replaces fallback rotation. Sector conflict: see top-level notes item 2. Father beat is a verbatim echo of sector 6 (ender 7), not a new sector. Sister beat extends her own already-established childhood memory (talking through the wall, thought it was the radio) rather than inventing a new fact.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: I still think about the wall, some nights. Him talking to something on the other side of it.
I used to think it was the radio. I know better now. I still like pretending, some nights.

beats.speaker: system
lines: SECTOR SCAN: NO NEW DATA.
ECHO FOLLOWS.

beats.speaker: father
lines: Again. You almost had me that time.
Do not go easy on me. If you learn to go easy, you will ruin the whole point.
One more game, then I open the shop.

items.notes: New, replaces fallback rotation. Sector conflict: see top-level notes item 2. Father beat is a verbatim echo of sector 4 (ender 5), not a new sector.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: I am done being scared of that room. I do not know what I am instead.
Ready, maybe. Or just tired of being scared. Some days those are the same thing.

beats.speaker: system
lines: SECTOR SCAN: NO NEW DATA.
ECHO FOLLOWS.

beats.speaker: father
lines: He is not ready yet. Keep the door shut.
Not until he can beat you square. Promise me.
No shortcuts. He will hate it. That is fine.

items.notes: New, replaces fallback rotation. Sector conflict: see top-level notes item 2. Father beat is a verbatim echo of sector 2, matching the CURRENT shipped run-end-3 lines exactly ('This bench light is the only one on the block... the shop and I have some talking to do'), not a new sector. Quiet, wistful full-circle closer for the 9-12 echo block.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Twelve times now. I stopped counting how many times you have gone in.
I started counting how close you are coming back out.

beats.speaker: system
lines: SECTOR SCAN: NO NEW DATA.
ECHO FOLLOWS.

beats.speaker: father
lines: This bench light is the only one on the block.
Go back to bed, kiddo. I will be up a while yet.
The shop and I have some talking to do.

items.notes: New. Plays before the scripted, unwinnable first dive. Chronologically before run-open-1's shop handoff; Rhea is catching the player at the curtain before proprietorship is even formal, which is what makes run-open-1's 'One rule' land as a reiteration.

beats.speaker: system
lines: BENCH TERMINAL: FIRST BOOT.
DAD.LOG: FOUND, UNOPENED.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Do not. I have not even given you the keys yet.
Whatever is back there, it can wait one more day. Can it not?

beats.speaker: system
lines: OVERRIDE ACCEPTED.
MANUAL DIVE INITIATED.

items.notes: New. Plays right after the scripted dive fails and the machine reseals, before run 1 day 1. Sets up the hard rule that run-open-1 then states as an established boundary.

beats.speaker: system
lines: CORE UNREACHED.
THE ROOM SEALS ITSELF AGAIN.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: You scared ten years off me just now.
Whatever Dad locked in there, it stays locked. Are we clear?

beats.speaker: system
lines: MORNING.
THE SHOP OPENS ANYWAY.

items.notes: Neutral shop-rhythm register, safe at any run count; see top-level notes item 3.

beats.speaker: system
lines: DAY 1.
SPIKE: THREE TICKETS.
REGISTER: OPEN.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Till is counted. Spike is loaded. Try not to break anything before lunch.
Yell if the fans start smelling like smoke.

beats.speaker: system
lines: THE CURTAIN AT THE BACK DOES NOT MOVE.
IT NEVER DOES.

items.notes: Matches existing DAY_LINES day 2 (strain carries over); no dayline change needed.

beats.speaker: system
lines: DAY 2.
STRAIN CARRIES OVER.
THE COFFEE DOES NOT.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Pot is fresh. Drink it before it is not.
The Kestrel courier drone is back. Same customer, new complaint.

items.notes: Matches existing DAY_LINES day 3 (word getting around, stranger tickets); no dayline change needed.

beats.speaker: system
lines: DAY 3.
WORD IS GETTING AROUND.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Somebody asked if we fix possessed machines now.
I told them we fix intrusions. They looked disappointed either way.

beats.speaker: system
lines: THE TICKET SPIKE IS GETTING TALLER.
SO IS THE LINE OUTSIDE.

items.notes: Matches existing DAY_LINES day 4 (intrusions pacing themselves); note this refers to ordinary customer jobs, not the back room, so it does not preempt Rhea's own run-4 ender pacing reveal.

beats.speaker: system
lines: DAY 4.
THE INTRUSIONS ARE PACING THEMSELVES.
WATCH FOR IT.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Ledger is balanced. Barely.
Four tickets came in already and it is not even ten.

items.notes: Matches existing DAY_LINES day 5 (halfway, back room quiet); no dayline change needed. Padlock still stays belief-neutral, physical only.

beats.speaker: system
lines: DAY 5.
HALFWAY.
THE BACK ROOM HAS BEEN QUIET. JUST QUIET.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Halfway through the book and the shop is still standing. Small miracles.
Eat something. I will not ask twice.

beats.speaker: system
lines: THE PADLOCK CATCHES THE LIGHT WHEN THE SUN COMES THROUGH THE CURTAIN.
STILL CLOSED.

items.notes: Matches existing DAY_LINES day 6 (coffee, three tickets, no excuses); no dayline change needed.

beats.speaker: system
lines: DAY 6.
THREE TICKETS. NO EXCUSES.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Coffee is on the bench. Drink it before it becomes a science experiment.
The Ledgerstone pawn vault sent someone over again. Good, they pay on time.

items.notes: Matches existing DAY_LINES day 7 (hard cases, take them anyway); no dayline change needed.

beats.speaker: system
lines: DAY 7.
THE HARD CASES ARE FINDING YOU.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Take them anyway. Hard cases pay better and complain less.
Three tickets. One of them looks like it bites.

items.notes: Matches existing DAY_LINES day 8 (strain as budget); no dayline change needed. Deliberately used a generic register drawer, not the canon shoebox of pharmacy receipts, to avoid preempting the run-4 RECEIPTS journal reveal.

beats.speaker: system
lines: DAY 8.
STRAIN IS A BUDGET.
SPEND IT LIKE RENT IS DUE.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: The register drawer is getting fat with customer receipts again.
Do the deposit before you dive into anything. Please.

items.notes: Matches existing DAY_LINES day 9 (last paying day, back room settles up tomorrow); no dayline change needed.

beats.speaker: system
lines: DAY 9.
LAST DAY OF PAYING WORK.
TOMORROW THE BACK ROOM SETTLES UP.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Last three tickets before the books close for the cycle.
Whatever is waiting for you tomorrow, it can wait one more day of customers first.

items.notes: New. Replaces the finale-door morning copy per the brief. No working day / no DAY_LINE needed for day 10 (contract only requires 9 entries, one per working day). Stays belief-neutral: uses only the established phrase 'the back room settles up', not a virus/Patch assertion, since this plays on every run's day 10 regardless of run count.

beats.speaker: system
lines: DAY 10.
NO TICKETS ON THE SPIKE.
THE BACK ROOM SETTLES UP TODAY.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: No customers today. Just you, the curtain, and that padlock.
I am not going to pretend I am fine with this. I am going to make coffee instead.

beats.speaker: system
lines: THE PADLOCK WAITS WHERE IT ALWAYS WAITS.
TODAY IT EITHER LETS GO OR IT DOES NOT.

beats.speaker: sister
lines: Go on, then.
I will be at the counter. Same as always.
